findings.title: Password verification can be bypassed when a backup code is submitted with an arbitrary totpCode
findings.body: In the credentials authorize flow, password verification is only performed when credentials.totpCode is absent. A client can send a valid backupCode together with any non-empty totpCode; the password check is skipped, and the new backup-code branch then authenticates the user if the backup code is valid. For password-based CAL accounts this allows a stolen backup code to be used without the account password. The password must be verified whenever password login is being used, including when a backup code is submitted.

findings.title: Backup codes are consumed with a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: During backup-code login, the encrypted backup-code array is decrypted, checked in memory, mutated, re-encrypted, and written back in a standalone Prisma update. Two concurrent login attempts using the same backup code can both read the array before either update commits, causing both to succeed and violating the one-time-use property. Concurrent use of different backup codes can also overwrite each other's updates and resurrect consumed codes. Consumption should be atomic, transactional, or modeled as individually hashed/unique codes.

findings.title: backupCode is used without validating that it is a string
findings.body: The disable endpoint calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "") without first validating that req.body.backupCode is a string. A JSON request body that supplies an object, array, number, or null for backupCode will throw a TypeError and produce a 500 instead of returning a validation error. Validate and normalize request fields before using string methods.

findings.title: Backup codes are not trimmed or lower-cased before comparison
findings.body: Generated backup codes are lowercase hex strings, but the login path only removes dashes before comparing. If a user types or pastes a code with surrounding whitespace or uppercase characters, the comparison fails even though the code is valid. The same issue exists in the disable endpoint. Input should be trimmed and lower-cased before comparison.

findings.title: Empty backup-code submission gives no user feedback
findings.body: The login form uses noValidate and the Zod schema does not validate backupCode. If the user is on the backup-code screen and submits an empty value, the server returns SecondFactorRequired because neither backupCode nor totpCode is present, and the handler only keeps twoFactorRequired true without setting an error message. The UI therefore appears to do nothing instead of telling the user a backup code is required.

findings.title: No automated test exercises backup-code login or disable-with-backup-code
findings.body: The added e2e coverage only checks that backup codes are displayed, downloadable, and copyable after enabling 2FA. It does not test the newly added authentication paths: logging in with a backup code via 'Lost access' or disabling 2FA using a backup code. These are security-critical flows and should have explicit tests.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes message is misleading during login
findings.body: The missing_backup_codes string says 'Please generate them in your settings.' This is not actionable when the message is shown on the login lost-access flow, because the user is locked out and cannot access settings. The message should state that no backup codes are available for this sign-in attempt.

findings.title: Closing the dialog after 2FA is enabled does not reset state or notify the parent
findings.body: EnableTwoFactorModal passes onOpenChange directly to Dialog. If the user dismisses the dialog via the close control or backdrop while the backup-code step is displayed after 2FA has already been enabled, neither resetState nor onEnable is called. If the modal remains mounted, reopening it can show stale state, and the parent settings screen is not notified that 2FA was enabled.
